# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 71 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 71 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_071_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Part 2 — The Meaning of the Rods

**71:1** "Those whose rods were found withered and moth-eaten — these are the apostates and betrayers of the church, who blasphemed the Lord in their sins and were also ashamed of the name of the Lord which was invoked upon them. These people are utterly dead to God. And you see that not one of them repented, even though they heard my words which you proclaimed to them. From such people life has departed."

**71:2** "But those who gave up their dry and cracked rods — they too are close to the apostates. They did not apostatize, but they never bore fruit. For just as a dry rod bears no fruit, so also these people live indeed, but carry no fruit of a good deed. Their repentance, however, is still possible for them, if they repent quickly. But if they delay, they too will share death with the first group."

**71:3** "Lord," I said, "why is repentance possible for them, but not for the first group? Their rods were similar." "For this reason," he said, "repentance is still possible for them — they did not blaspheme their Lord, nor become betrayers of the church. But through the desire for gain, they deceived and each one served his own desires. Let them repent, therefore."

**71:4** "Those who gave up their rods half-dry and cracked — listen to them. Those who are always double-minded and who speak ill of one another are the ones whose rods were half-dry. Many of them repented when they heard my commandments, and those who repented had their dwelling place in the first tower. But those who repented more slowly had their dwelling in the second tower."

**71:5** "Those who gave up their rods green but with dried tips — these are those who were faithful but rich, and who were immersed in the affairs of the world. They are ashamed of the truth. Some of them when they heard my commandments repented and were found good. The rest remain even now in their affairs and are severed from the holy ones. These will find the place of the third tower difficult."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the systematic rod-interpretation framework of Similitude 8.*
